status_summary: ETA proposed on 2025-07-01 to remove the requirement that states use state merit staff for Wagner-Peyser Employment Service work, and on 2026-01-21 it delayed the 2023 rule's compliance date by one year to 2027-01-21. A final rule published 2026-08-20 (91 FR 54024) removes the merit-staffing provision in 20 CFR 652.215 so that each state may choose its staffing model, and it took effect on 2026-10-19. On 2026-09-10 AFSCME sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking vacatur of the rule and an injunction; no stay, injunction, ruling or later Federal Register document affecting the rule was found as of 2026-10-25, and codification by Congress was not found.

timeline.event: ETA published a proposed rule to remove the state merit staff requirement for Wagner-Peyser Employment Service staffing.
ETA delayed the compliance date of the 2023 merit staffing rule by one year, to 2027-01-21.
ETA published a final rule deleting the merit staffing requirement (20 CFR 652.215), effective 2026-10-19.

AFSCME filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (No. 1:26-cv-03162) against the Labor Department, claiming under the Administrative Procedure Act that the final rule is contrary to law and arbitrary, and seeking vacatur and an injunction against its implementation; the complaint does not request a stay under section 705.
